name: Git
description: Version control with Git: commits, branches, merging and rebasing, collaboration on GitHub-style platforms, and Git internals.

nodes.name: Why version control
nodes.desc: What version control solves, snapshots, and centralised vs distributed systems.
nodes.summary: You will understand what problems version control solves and how centralised and distributed systems differ in the way they store history.

nodes.name: Git basics
nodes.desc: init, add, commit, status and the working tree, index and repository.
nodes.summary: You will be able to create a repository, stage changes and record commits while understanding the working tree, index and repository.
topics: Initialising a repository with git init

nodes.name: History & undo
nodes.desc: log, diff, show, restore, reset and revert.
nodes.summary: You will be able to inspect project history and safely undo changes at the file, staging and commit level.

nodes.name: Ignoring & config
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep unwanted files out of a repository and configure Git with identity settings and aliases.

nodes.name: Branches
nodes.desc: Creating and switching branches and what a branch really is.
nodes.summary: You will understand that a branch is a movable pointer to a commit and be able to create, switch and delete branches.

nodes.name: Merging
nodes.summary: You will be able to combine branches with git merge and predict whether Git performs a fast-forward or a three-way merge.
topics: Three-way merges and the merge base

nodes.name: Merge conflicts
nodes.desc: Reading and resolving conflicts and using merge tools.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read conflict markers, resolve conflicting changes by hand or with a merge tool, and complete the merge.

nodes.name: Rebasing
nodes.desc: Rebase, interactive rebase and when not to rewrite history.
nodes.summary: You will be able to replay commits onto a new base, tidy history with interactive rebase and know when rewriting history is unsafe.
topics: Replaying commits onto a new base
The golden rule of not rebasing shared history

nodes.name: Remotes
nodes.desc: clone, fetch, pull, push and tracking branches.
nodes.summary: You will be able to clone repositories and synchronise work with remotes using fetch, pull and push with tracking branches.

nodes.name: Pull requests
nodes.desc: Forks, pull requests, code review and keeping a branch up to date.
nodes.summary: You will be able to contribute through forks and pull requests, respond to code review and keep a branch current with its base.
topics: Updating a branch with merge or rebase

nodes.name: Branching workflows
nodes.desc: Trunk-based development, feature branches and release branches.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare common team branching strategies and choose one that fits a project's release cadence.

nodes.name: Open-source PR project
nodes.desc: Find an open-source project, fork it and land a real pull request.
nodes.summary: You will land a real pull request in an open-source project, from finding an issue to getting the change merged.
topics: Forking, branching and committing a fix

nodes.name: Objects & refs
nodes.desc: Blobs, trees, commits and refs: the commit graph as a content-addressed DAG.
nodes.summary: You will understand how Git stores data as content-addressed objects and how refs point into the commit graph.
topics: The commit graph as a DAG

nodes.name: Bisect & reflog
nodes.desc: Recovering lost work with reflog and finding regressions with bisect.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recover commits that seem lost using the reflog and locate the commit that introduced a bug with bisect.
topics: How the reflog records HEAD movements
Binary search over history with git bisect
Automating bisect with a test script

nodes.name: Stash & cherry-pick
nodes.desc: Stashing work in progress, cherry-picking and worktrees.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set aside unfinished work, copy individual commits between branches and work on several branches at once.

nodes.name: Hooks
nodes.desc: Client-side hooks for linting and tests before commit.
nodes.summary: You will be able to automate checks such as linting and tests by writing client-side Git hooks that run before commits.
topics: Sharing hooks with a hook manager

nodes.name: Submodules & monorepos
nodes.summary: You will be able to manage code from multiple projects using submodules, subtrees or a monorepo and handle very large repositories.
